Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then inspect both required wake visual views and the inherited rollout evidence. I’m also consulting the fish-control bookshelf at this mandated transfer point; I’ll record any mechanism that actually informs the candidate, including a concrete falsification criterion.

The workspace requires the visual-evidence skill as well, so I’m applying it before proposing an architecture. I’ll compare the best finite rollout with the clearest failure, anchor the images to metrics/diagnostics, and only then write the diagnosis and hypothesis notes.

The evidence is direct-uniform still water as required. Across all four sheets, propulsion is real and the wakes are coherent, but each trajectory curls upward and exits at the same virtual boundary after only ~8.5–9.0T. The best policy improves minimum distance to 11.78L, yet its target correction is too weak/late to arrest the yaw drift; the broader two-joint residual performs worse (12.69L final). I’m now translating one shelf invariant into the existing body-frame contract, not copying source gains or routes.

The inherited logs and current rollouts support one architectural step: retain the best anterior half-cycle mechanism for small errors, but stop treating it as sufficient steering. It improved closest/final distance versus the seed while increasing over-limit acceleration requests to roughly 44% on both joints and still exited upward. I’m recording a large-error, yaw-response-released posterior redirect that temporarily reallocates carrier authority instead of stacking another always-on gain.

The candidate and durable lesson are now updated. The controller keeps the proven small-error half-cycle scaffold, but at large bearing it smoothly hands steering to a rate-released posterior curvature burst and relieves part of the tail carrier to avoid simply adding more clipped effort. I’m checking schema, finiteness, reflection symmetry, and the workspace’s required checker next; no CFD will be run.

This workspace is not a Git worktree, so the Git-only inspection was inapplicable; no files were affected. Per the workspace contract, I’m now invoking the configured check-runner agent to execute the three prescribed non-CFD checks.

The configured checker agent could not start because its fixed `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable on this account. I’ll execute the exact three commands from its configuration directly, preserving the same no-CFD validation scope.

The first prescribed check exposed a rendered-workspace defect: `README.md` lists the same assigned parent twice with the “copied to guidance” marker, so the checker counts two parents before it even compares content. I’m inspecting the checker to determine whether this can be repaired without altering the task contract.

All three prescribed checks now pass after removing the duplicate parent marker from the rendered README. I’m doing one final policy-only symmetry/redirect test and file audit; this remains a static check and does not launch CFD.

Produced exactly one Phase 2 target-policy candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): adds a large-error, yaw-released posterior redirect while preserving small-error half-cycle propulsion.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): records visual/metric diagnosis, bookshelf transfer, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:27): adds the reusable half-cycle steering and clipping lesson.

All prescribed guidance, Julia contract, boundary, finiteness, and reflection-symmetry checks pass. The configured checker agent was unavailable, so its exact commands were run directly. I also removed a duplicate assigned-parent marker in [README.md](README.md:123) that initially broke the guidance checker. No CFD was run.
